introduction: The Massachusetts earned income tax credit is claimed on a state income tax return. It can reduce tax and produce a refund for qualifying workers, including some who are not otherwise required to file.

who: Workers meeting the applicable federal EITC requirements and Massachusetts tax rules.
Residents for at least part of the tax year; people who are nonresidents for the entire year cannot claim it.
Filing status, qualifying children, Social Security numbers and income affect eligibility. Special filing exceptions require careful review.
sections.get: A refundable state tax credit based on the federal credit. The state lists 40% for tax years beginning in 2023 or later; part-year residents must prorate.
sections.docs: Prepare wage and self-employment records, Social Security numbers, child residency records if relevant, federal return and Massachusetts residency dates. Keep records supporting a child claim if another person may claim the child.
sections.apply:
1. Use the Department of Revenue guidance for the tax year being filed.
  2. Determine the federal EITC and complete the Massachusetts resident or part-year return.
  3. Claim the state credit even if filing only to request this refund.
  4. Ask a VITA or Tax-Aide preparer for help if available.
sections.after: Save both returns and monitor refund or document requests. If the IRS later changes the federal EITC, review whether an amended Massachusetts return is required.

faqs: Must I file a Massachusetts return?
Yes, the state credit must be claimed on a Massachusetts return.
Eligible part-year residents prorate the credit by their Massachusetts residency period.
Some can, subject to the applicable age and other federal and state criteria.
Can I use last year’s income limits?
Use the guidance for the year of the return; limits change.
